findings.summary: A book point is missing from these pages.
findings.evidence: Case study: design a Zomato/Swiggy-style three-sided marketplace (customers, restaurants, delivery partners)

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a flat description with no hook that gives a scroller a reason to keep reading.
findings.evidence: "An end-to-end system design case study of a Zomato/Swiggy-style food delivery app."
findings.fix: Open with a hook such as "How does Swiggy get a hot biryani to your door in 30 minutes? Here's the full system design, from search to live tracking." and keep the topic list after it.

findings.summary: The State Machine diagram has overlapping and clipped state labels and edge labels.
findings.evidence: State nodes read "PAYMENT_PEI" (clipped by the PLACED node), "PREPARING" and "CREATED" touch their pill borders, and "READY" is overprinted by the edge label "no accept, 3 min", so it reads "no accept,READY3 min".
findings.fix: Widen the diagram or switch to a two-row layout with larger node spacing. Shorten the node labels, for example PAYMENT_PENDING to PENDING. Move the "no accept 3 min" label off the READY node.

findings.summary: The compare-and-set idea behind the order state machine is used as shorthand ("racer", "CAS") before it is ever explained.
findings.evidence: The SQL note says "0 rows means a racer won" and the data model row says "version | int | **CAS** counter". The term "compare-and-set" appears only in the closing takeaway: "Every state move is a compare-and-set".
findings.fix: Add a one-line explanation before the SQL block: two events can race to move the same order, so each update names the status it expects and bumps version. Spell out CAS = compare-and-set there. Put the SQL after the state machine, and define version before the SQL uses it.

findings.summary: Text overflows its shapes in the Per-Event Flow diagram.
findings.evidence: "Event arrives" is cut by the circle outline, so it reads "Event" / "arrives" crossing the border. "Seen (order_id, event_type)?" extends past the right slope of the diamond.
findings.fix: Enlarge the circle and diamond, or shorten the labels to "Event" and "Seen before?".

findings.summary: The order-lifecycle flow skips the READY state that the Order Service state machine defines.
findings.evidence: nodes: ["PLACED","ACCEPTED","PREPARING","PICKED_UP","DELIVERED"] (page 5 has PREPARING -> READY -> PICKED_UP)
findings.fix: Add READY between PREPARING and PICKED_UP so both diagrams show the same lifecycle.

findings.summary: The claim that writes need sharding is overstated for ~300 QPS of order writes. A single Postgres primary handles that comfortably.
findings.evidence: "Reads scale with **caches** and replicas; writes need sharding" (peak writes ~300 QPS)
findings.fix: Say that order writes fit on one primary with replicas, and that sharding (or a separate store) is only needed for the 60K/s GPS stream and for long-term growth.

findings.summary: Kafka is referenced before the architecture page introduces it.
findings.evidence: "GPS pings need their own Kafka-backed path". Kafka is first introduced on page 3: "==Async== (Kafka) for side effects".
findings.fix: Say "a separate streaming path" on page 2, or add "(Kafka, introduced next page)".

findings.summary: The first block bundles the failure handling and metrics (timeout auto-cancel, duplicate create) ahead of the design and state machine they refer to.

findings.summary: "Batching" is used for two different things, and the first use is not explained.
findings.evidence: The filter step says "Filter: status, capacity, batching" and the data model says "current_orders ... batching load limit", meaning several orders per rider. The callout says "Batching every 2-5 s with the Hungarian algorithm", meaning batch matching.
findings.fix: Call the first one "multi-order capacity" or "order stacking", and keep "batch matching" for the 2-5 s matching window. Add one line explaining the Hungarian algorithm and H3.

findings.summary: Assignment depends on a live rider-location index that is only explained on the next page.

findings.fix: Add a note on page 8 that the index is fed by the GPS pings described in Real-Time Tracking, or place Tracking ingestion before Assignment.
